text: Continuous Integration (CI) is a common practice in modern software development. Developers regularly add their code to a shared repository, and each change triggers automated builds. This means the software is compiled automatically, so the team can see immediately whether the new code works. During the build, the system also runs tests to check that nothing has broken. By doing this, teams catch issues early, when they are easier and cheaper to fix. A CI pipeline usually includes these steps: building, testing, and reporting results. This process helps teams work faster and with more confidence, because problems are found before they reach users.
